# Can a blind selector recognize expert rewrites on held-out Bridge problems?

The 482-pair test release labels the expert revision as preferred to the original novice response. The earlier MRBench endpoint was full guidance among six identified generators. This experiment tests a different task. The author's test row labels have not been scored locally when writing this protocol. Use the published 8,136-pair training release. No test tuning. Exclude blank problems, exact shared normalized problems with fitting or earlier MRBench openings, exact shared nonempty response text with fitting or earlier MRBench responses, and duplicates of the same unordered pair for the same problem. Count excluded rows and number of remaining unique normalized problems. This detects literal overlap. Semantic paraphrases can remain.

The candidate is a linear pairwise preference ranker on concatenated TF-IDF word unigrams/bigrams and character boundary ngrams of length 3–5. Fit vocabulary on training responses only, min_df 2, sublinear counts. Fit balanced signed differences of chosen-minus-other features and their negatives using logistic regression with fixed C=1 and no intercept. Lexically sort alternatives for blind tie-breaking. Controls are word-only and character-only versions, longer response, more questions, and fixed lexicographic first. Include the always-expert role policy as a fixed-tutor control for a user who knows the two roles. Report it as an identity-informed ceiling, not an attainable blind policy. Include the EMNLP 2025 authors' scaffolding reward model in the registry. Run it on the identical rows only if the candidate passes the cheaper blind controls. An earlier failure rules out superiority and the larger-model contrast remains explicitly unevaluated. Each comparison must exceed one percentage point and have a positive simultaneous 95% lower bound from 10,000 paired normalized-problem bootstrap draws, seed 731. Save anonymized per-row correctness for replay. Systematic preference for expert edits precludes strict superiority over the role-aware fixed policy. The blind ranking endpoint cannot rescue that original identity-aware claim.
